Summary  
Data source overview: The paper introduces “prompt tuning,” a method that learns small, continuous “soft-prompt” vectors—rather than updating all model weights—to condition a frozen large language model (LLM) for new tasks. Experiments on the T5 family show that, for models above one billion parameters, prompt tuning can match full fine-tuning performance while also exhibiting greater robustness to domain shift.  
EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83] – High confidence that the knowledge fabric captures every causal–interventional pathway in the abstract. The abstract is short, so some connections (e.g. causes of robustness) required moderate inference, reflected in lower edge-confidence scores.  
Inference strategy justification: Where the abstract implied but did not explicitly spell out mechanisms (e.g. why robustness improves), moderate inference (edge confidence = 2) was used, consistent with the instructions for lightly inferred links.  
Extraction completeness explanation: All distinct claims (risks, problem analyses, insights, design choices, mechanisms, evidence, interventions) that appear or are implied in the abstract are represented as nodes, with shared nodes inter-connecting both risk pathways into a single fabric—no isolated nodes remain.  
Key limitations: 1) Only the abstract was available; deeper sections could reveal additional evidence or interventions. 2) Edge confidence is capped by limited details; future full-paper extraction would strengthen validation edges. 3) Deployment-phase intervention maturity is estimated; real-world adoption data would improve accuracy.
